summary: Eikan Taki works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Taki is a member of Taisho University and was attested as a lecturer at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute in 2006.

Eiki Hoshino studied at Taisho University from circa 1962 to 1970. Working in religious and Buddhist studies, he served as a professor in the Faculty of Humanities and as a director at Taisho University from around 1980 to 2013.
Eiko Okukaze is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a doctoral student at Bukkyo University (attested 2010). Okukaze is attested as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University in 2026.

Eileen M. Dimes earned a B.A. from the University of London in 1932. Active in Indology, she worked in the library at SOAS in 1945 and succeeded Alfred Master in 1959 as Assistant Keeper for Modern Indian languages at the India Office Records.

Eileen Power was an historian educated at Oxford High School, Girton College, Cambridge (ca. 1907–1910), and the University of Paris (ca. 1910–1911). She held posts at the London School of Economics (ca. 1921–1940) and the University of London (ca. 1931–1940).

Eilhard Mitscherlich studied at Heidelberg, Paris (under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy), Göttingen, Berlin, and Stockholm. Active in Iranian/Central Asian studies and chemistry, he held posts at Frederick William University Berlin (ca. 1821–1863) and Humboldt University.

Eino Wälikangas studied at the University of Helsinki (M.A. ca. 1908–1914) under doctoral supervisor J. N. Reuter. Working in Indology and linguistics, he taught Sanskrit at the University of Helsinki from circa 1915 to 1918.

Eisaku Okada studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014) and works in Buddhist studies. Okada has held positions at the JSPS (2014), Kyoto University (2015), and Koyasan University (commissioned researcher in 2014; specially appointed lecturer in 2026).
Eisei Kojima was a Buddhist studies scholar who, in 1976, was attested as a professor at Ryukoku University and president of Doho University.

Eishu Miyazaki, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, studied at Rissho University (ca. 1933–1936) and under Gyoo Kageyama. He held posts at Minobusan University and Rissho University (ca. 1950–1984).
Eishun Fushimi is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson (attested 1998).

Eivind Kahrs studied under Nils Simonsson, working in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held a post at Queens' College (attested 2010), taught Aleix Ruiz-Falqués, and serves as a Council member of the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).
Eiyin Yasuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1957 to 1961 and trained under Gyōin Hashimoto from circa 1950 to 1978.
Eizan Tatsuta was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sokatsu Shaku and founded Ningen Zen.

Ekai Kawaguchi studied at Gyōsei Shoin, Doshisha, Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College, under teachers including Enryo Inoue and Sarat Chandra Das. He served as rector of Gohyaku Rakan-ji and professor at Toyo University (1916).
Ekkyo Uno is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji Sōgakuin (attested 1998).

Elaine Fisher studied as a doctoral student at Columbia University, where she was later a PhD candidate (attested 2013). Working in Indology and religious studies, she became an Assistant Professor at Stanford University in 2017.

Eleanor Nesbitt studied at Girton College, Cambridge, Oxford, and the University of Warwick (PhD 1995). A scholar of religious studies and Indology, she became Emeritus Professor at Warwick (attested 1996) and co-founded the Punjab Research Group and a journal.

Eleanor Rosch studied at Reed College and Harvard University (Ph.D. under Roger Brown). Working in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and cognitive psychology, she held posts at Brown University, Connecticut College, and the University of California, Berkeley (appointed 1971).

Elena Bashir earned her degree at the University of Michigan in 1988, where she later lectured (ca. 1997–2004). Specializing in linguistics and Indology, she held posts at the University of Chicago, becoming Senior Lecturer Emerita around 2020.
